signatures.member: public static float getDamageAfterAbsorb(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity, float, net.minecraft.world.damagesource.DamageSource, float, float)
signatures.notes: public static, client-callable. Params: (victim, damage, source, totalArmor, armorToughness). Body: toughness = 2.0F + armorToughness/4.0F; realArmor = Mth.clamp(totalArmor - damage/toughness, totalArmor*0.2F, 20.0F); armorFraction = realArmor/25.0F; then ONLY if source.getWeaponItem()!=null && victim.level() instanceof ServerLevel does it call EnchantmentHelper.modifyArmorEffectiveness(...) clamped to [0,1]; return damage * (1.0F - modifiedArmorFraction). On a client level that branch is skipped, so the client result equals the server result whenever no Breach-style armor-effectiveness enchantment is involved. For explosions getWeaponItem() is null anyway (directEntity is null or not an item holder).

public static, client-callable. Params: (damage, totalMagicArmor). Body: realArmor = Mth.clamp(totalMagicArmor, 0.0F, 20.0F); return damage * (1.0F - realArmor/25.0F). EPF caps at 20 -> max 80% reduction.

There is NO getArmorToughness() on 26.2. Armour toughness is only reachable as (float) getAttributeValue(Attributes.ARMOR_TOUGHNESS) — exactly what LivingEntity.getDamageAfterArmorAbsorb does. Client-callable.

On LivingEntity this reads a plain non-synced field, so for a non-player entity the client always sees 0. Player OVERRIDES it (see next entry) to read synched entity data, so it is correct for the local player.
Override: return (Float)this.getEntityData().get(DATA_PLAYER_ABSORPTION_ID). Fully synced -> reliable client-side for LocalPlayer.
Clamps via Mth.clamp(x, 0.0F, this.getMaxAbsorption()). Do not call client-side; listed to explain why the double decrement in LivingEntity.actuallyHurt is a no-op.

final. Body: (float) getAttributeValue(Attributes.MAX_ABSORPTION). Client-callable.

PROTECTED — not callable from outside the class hierarchy without an accessor/mixin. Body: if (!damageSource.is(DamageTypeTags.BYPASSES_ARMOR)) { hurtArmor(...); damage = CombatRules.getDamageAfterAbsorb(this, damage, damageSource, this.getArmorValue(), (float)this.getAttributeValue(Attributes.ARMOR_TOUGHNESS)); } return damage;
PROTECTED. Contains the resistance arithmetic and the ServerLevel-gated EnchantmentHelper.getDamageProtection call (falls back to enchantmentArmor = 0.0F on a client level).

SERVER-ONLY (takes ServerLevel) and protected. Order: armor absorb -> magic absorb -> absorption soak -> setHealth. Absorption soak: float toHealth = Math.max(dmg - getAbsorptionAmount(), 0.0F); setAbsorptionAmount(getAbsorptionAmount() - (dmg - toHealth)); if (toHealth != 0) { recordDamage; setHealth(getHealth() - toHealth); setAbsorptionAmount(getAbsorptionAmount() - toHealth); }  — that last line is a no-op because absorption is already 0 and setAbsorptionAmount clamps to >= 0.
SERVER-ONLY. Player's override does NOT re-subtract absorption a second time, and adds causeFoodExhaustion(source.getFoodExhaustion()). Same absorb-then-health math otherwise.

SERVER-ONLY. This is where the invulnerability-tick logic lives: if (this.invulnerableTime > 10.0F && !source.is(DamageTypeTags.BYPASSES_COOLDOWN)) { if (damage <= this.lastHurt) return false; actuallyHurt(level, source, damage - this.lastHurt); this.lastHurt = damage; } else { this.lastHurt = damage; this.invulnerableTime = 20; actuallyHurt(level, source, damage); }. There is NO client-side hurt() entry point on 26.2.

SERVER-ONLY. Difficulty scaling lives HERE, before super: if (source.scalesWithDifficulty()) { PEACEFUL -> damage = 0; EASY -> damage = Math.min(damage/2.0F + 1.0F, damage); HARD -> damage = damage * 3.0F / 2.0F; } and returns false when abilities.invulnerable && !source.is(BYPASSES_INVULNERABILITY).

CLIENT-side handler (ClientPacketListener.handleDamageEvent -> entity.handleDamageEvent(packet.getSource(this.level))). Sets this.invulnerableTime = 20, hurtDuration = 10, hurtTime = 10. It does NOT set lastHurt.

PUBLIC mutable field, meaningfully tracked on the client for the local player: set to 20 in handleDamageEvent and decremented in LivingEntity.tick's `if (this.invulnerableTime > 0 && !(this instanceof ServerPlayer))` branch (that branch is OUTSIDE the isClientSide gate).

PROTECTED and NEVER set client-side (only in hurtServer). The client's copy is always 0, so the client cannot reproduce the `damage - lastHurt` i-frame partial-damage path. This is the single biggest source of client/server divergence for a damage estimator.
Takes a Holder, not a MobEffect. Client-callable; reads activeEffects, populated by ClientPacketListener.handleUpdateMobEffect.

SERVER-ONLY — first param is ServerLevel. NOT client-callable. Iterates all EquipmentSlot.VALUES and sums via Enchantment.modifyDamageProtection into a MutableFloat.
SERVER-ONLY. Needs ServerLevel purely to build the LootContext (Enchantment.damageContext -> new LootParams.Builder(serverLevel)) used to evaluate ConditionalEffect.requirements().

CLIENT-CALLABLE. Second param is ItemInstance on 26.2, NOT ItemStack — ItemStack implements ItemInstance so passing a stack still compiles. Body: piece.getOrDefault(DataComponents.ENCHANTMENTS, ItemEnchantments.EMPTY).getLevel(enchantment). This is the best client-side proxy for protection.

CLIENT-CALLABLE (no ServerLevel). Returns the HIGHEST single-piece level across the enchantment's own slots, not the sum — so it is wrong for Protection/Blast Protection EPF, which sums across the 4 armour pieces. Use getItemEnchantmentLevel per slot instead.
CLIENT-CALLABLE. Lets you read the data-driven values off the synced enchantment registry. Pair with EnchantmentEffectComponents.DAMAGE_PROTECTION.
Client-visible constant.
CLIENT-CALLABLE. Also public boolean matches(net.minecraft.world.level.storage.loot.LootContext) — that one is effectively server-only because building the LootContext requires a ServerLevel.

Members: on_fire, in_wall, cramming, drown, fly_into_wall, generic, wither, dragon_breath, starve, fall, ender_pearl, freeze, stalagmite, magic, indirect_magic, out_of_world, generic_kill, sonic_boom, outside_border.
Shipped tag = [fireworks, explosion, player_explosion, bad_respawn_point]. This is the tag Blast Protection's requirements predicate tests.
Has NO vanilla members — DamageTypeTagsProvider never adds to it. So every damage type, explosions included, is subject to the 10-tick i-frame partial-damage rule.

Client-callable via Level (Level implements LevelAccessor). Body: this.getLevelData().getDifficulty(); ClientLevel.ClientLevelData holds a real, server-synced Difficulty with setDifficulty from the change-difficulty packet.
Client-visible constant, but see the DEATH_PROTECTION entry — the item identity is NOT what vanilla checks.

THIS is the real trigger on 26.2. LivingEntity.checkTotemDeathProtection is `private` (server-only path), but its condition is fully reproducible client-side: !killingDamage.is(DamageTypeTags.BYPASSES_INVULNERABILITY) AND one of getItemInHand(MAIN_HAND)/getItemInHand(OFF_HAND) has a non-null DEATH_PROTECTION component. On success it does setHealth(1.0F) and consumes one item. Components are synced, so the check is reachable client-side.
Record with List<ConsumeEffect> deathEffects(). Client-visible.
PRIVATE — not callable at all from outside. Reimplement the condition (see DEATH_PROTECTION entry) rather than trying to reach it.
Client-callable. Armour slots are EquipmentSlot.HEAD/CHEST/LEGS/FEET (EquipmentSlot also has MAINHAND, OFFHAND, BODY, SADDLE, and a public static final List<EquipmentSlot> VALUES).
Client-callable — use for the totem check.

@Nullable, PUBLIC, client-callable. Returns useItem only if it has DataComponents.BLOCKS_ATTACKS and elapsedTicks >= blocksAttacks.blockDelayTicks(). Also public boolean isBlocking() = getItemBlockingWith() != null.

PUBLIC and client-callable (params: source, dealtDamage, angleRadians). Sums DamageReduction.resolve then Mth.clamp(blocked, 0, dealtDamage). Vanilla shield = new BlocksAttacks(0.25F, 1.0F, List.of(new DamageReduction(90.0F, Optional.empty(), 0.0F, 1.0F)), new ItemDamageFunction(3.0F,1.0F,1.0F), Optional.of(BYPASSES_SHIELD), ...) -> blocks 100% of damage within a 90-degree frontal cone, and explosion is NOT in bypasses_shield, so a raised shield fully negates blast damage from the front.

SERVER-ONLY wrapper around resolveBlockedDamage. To model shields client-side, call BlocksAttacks.resolveBlockedDamage yourself with angle = Math.acos(horizontalNormalize(sourcePos - playerPos) dot calculateViewVector(0, getYHeadRot())).

signatures.member: public static float clamp(float, float, float)
signatures.notes: Client-callable helper used throughout the damage path.
Needed as the RandomSource argument to EnchantmentValueEffect.process.

Public field. Also `public net.minecraft.client.multiplayer.ClientLevel level;` and `public static net.minecraft.client.Minecraft getInstance()`. LocalPlayer extends AbstractClientPlayer extends Player extends LivingEntity.
Public field, reached via Player.getAbilities(). Synced (creative/spectator). Short-circuits all damage unless BYPASSES_INVULNERABILITY.

gotchas: CombatRules.getDamageAfterAbsorb now takes FIVE args including the victim and the DamageSource: (LivingEntity, float damage, DamageSource, float totalArmor, float armorToughness). A caller written against the old 3-arg (damage, armor, toughness) form will not compile.
There is no getArmorToughness() on LivingEntity. Toughness is only available as (float) livingEntity.getAttributeValue(Attributes.ARMOR_TOUGHNESS). getArmorValue() returns int (floored), not float.

MobEffects.RESISTANCE is a Holder<MobEffect>, and hasEffect/getEffect take Holder<MobEffect>. Code that passed a bare MobEffect/StatusEffect will not compile. Attributes.* are likewise Holder<Attribute>.

Resistance is NOT a flat 20%-per-level multiply of the modern form some code assumes; the exact 26.2 arithmetic in LivingEntity.getDamageAfterMagicAbsorb is: int absorbValue = (amplifier + 1) * 5; int absorb = 25 - absorbValue; damage = Math.max(damage * absorb / 25.0F, 0.0F). Amplifier is 0-based, so Resistance V (amplifier 4) yields absorb == 0 and total immunity. It is gated on !source.is(BYPASSES_EFFECTS) and !source.is(BYPASSES_RESISTANCE), and it runs AFTER armour, not before.

EnchantmentHelper.getDamageProtection's first parameter is a ServerLevel, so it is flatly uncallable from client code — and LivingEntity.getDamageAfterMagicAbsorb silently substitutes enchantmentArmor = 0.0F when level() is not a ServerLevel. Any client-side estimator that just calls the vanilla path will therefore under-report protection to zero. Same for EnchantmentHelper.modifyArmorEffectiveness, isImmuneToDamage, modifyDamage, tickEffects, and Enchantment.modifyDamageProtection.

There IS still a client-callable route to the data-driven protection value, contrary to the usual assumption: Registries.ENCHANTMENT is in RegistryDataLoader.SYNCHRONIZED_REGISTRIES with Enchantment.DIRECT_CODEC, so the client holds full effect definitions. holder.value().getEffects(EnchantmentEffectComponents.DAMAGE_PROTECTION) then ConditionalEffect.effect().process(level, random, value) needs no ServerLevel. What you CANNOT evaluate is ConditionalEffect.requirements() — a LootItemCondition needing a LootContext built from a ServerLevel — so you must decide applicability yourself (for Blast Protection: source.is(DamageTypeTags.IS_EXPLOSION) && !source.is(DamageTypeTags.BYPASSES_INVULNERABILITY); for Protection: just !source.is(BYPASSES_INVULNERABILITY)).

EnchantmentHelper.getEnchantmentLevel(Holder, LivingEntity) is client-callable but returns the MAXIMUM single-piece level, not the sum across armour pieces. Using it for Protection/Blast Protection EPF silently under-counts by up to 4x. getDamageProtection sums over every EquipmentSlot, so you must loop HEAD/CHEST/LEGS/FEET with getItemEnchantmentLevel per stack.

EnchantmentHelper.getItemEnchantmentLevel's second parameter is net.minecraft.world.item.ItemInstance now, not ItemStack (ItemStack implements ItemInstance, so existing call sites still compile — but a mixin/handle signature written as (Holder, ItemStack) will not resolve).

Explosions do NOT bypass armour on 26.2 — verified from the shipped data/minecraft/tags/damage_type/bypasses_armor.json, which omits explosion and player_explosion. They also do not bypass effects, resistance, enchantments, cooldown, or shields. They ARE in is_explosion and no_knockback.

Explosion and player_explosion both carry scaling = "always" (DamageScaling.ALWAYS), so Player.hurtServer's difficulty scaling always applies to the local player: PEACEFUL -> 0, EASY -> min(d/2 + 1, d), HARD -> d * 3/2, NORMAL unchanged. This happens BEFORE armour, and mc.level.getDifficulty() is genuinely synced, so it is cheap to model — omitting it makes every HARD-difficulty estimate 33% low.

DamageTypeTags.BYPASSES_COOLDOWN has zero vanilla members, so the 10-tick invulnerability rule applies to explosions. But LivingEntity.lastHurt is only ever assigned in hurtServer, never in the client's handleDamageEvent, so the client's lastHurt is permanently 0 and the `actuallyHurt(damage - lastHurt)` partial-damage branch cannot be reproduced. invulnerableTime itself IS usable client-side (handleDamageEvent sets it to 20, and LivingEntity.tick decrements it outside the isClientSide gate) — so you can tell you are in i-frames, you just cannot tell how much damage the server will subtract. Treat invulnerableTime > 10 as "estimate is an upper bound of unknown tightness".

Absorption is a plain unsynced field on LivingEntity but Player OVERRIDES getAbsorptionAmount()/internalSetAbsorptionAmount to use DATA_PLAYER_ABSORPTION_ID synched data. So it is reliable for the local player and always 0 on the client for non-player mobs — do not reuse a player-tuned estimator for mobs.

Armour attribute modifiers from worn gear are applied only server-side: LivingEntity.detectEquipmentUpdates (which calls collectEquipmentChanges, the thing that addTransientModifier's item modifiers) sits inside `if (!this.level().isClientSide())`. The client's correct ARMOR/ARMOR_TOUGHNESS come from ClientboundUpdateAttributesPacket instead. That is fine for reading, but means you must not expect the client to derive armour from the equipped stacks itself, and there can be a one-tick lag right after an armour swap.

A raised shield fully negates explosion damage from the front on 26.2 and this is easy to miss: applyItemBlocking runs before armour in hurtServer, explosion is absent from bypasses_shield, and the vanilla shield's DamageReduction is (90-degree cone, no type filter, base 0.0, factor 1.0) = 100% blocked. The server-only wrapper is applyItemBlocking(ServerLevel, ...) but BlocksAttacks.resolveBlockedDamage and LivingEntity.getItemBlockingWith()/isBlocking() are both public and client-callable, so model it.

Totem of Undying is not an item check any more. LivingEntity.checkTotemDeathProtection is private and looks for DataComponents.DEATH_PROTECTION on either hand's stack, gated on !killingDamage.is(DamageTypeTags.BYPASSES_INVULNERABILITY); on success it sets health to 1.0F and shrinks the stack. Comparing against Items.TOTEM_OF_UNDYING works for vanilla but misses any datapack item carrying the component. Note the totem check runs only after isDeadOrDying(), i.e. after health already hit 0.

There is no client-side hurt()/damage() entry point at all: the whole pipeline is hurtServer(ServerLevel, ...) / actuallyHurt(ServerLevel, ...), and getDamageAfterArmorAbsorb / getDamageAfterMagicAbsorb are protected. A client estimator must reimplement the sequence rather than call into it.
